2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant Nos. 1-3 from making any sort of disturbance in his on going functions as a Nikah Registrar in the area of Golmunda Union Parishad contending, inter-alia, that the plaintiff is the permanent Marriage and Divorce Registrar for the area of Golmunda Union Parishad under Jaldhaka Police Station, District: Nilphamary. The plaintiff was appointed Nikah and Divorce Registrar on temporary basis for the aforesaid area vide Memo No. 370 /Bichar-7/2.L-84 /83 dated 1-6-2003 issued by the Trial section No. 7 of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. Sub-sequently he was appointed for the same permanently for the aforesaid area vide Memo No. 485/Bichar-7/2 N 84/83 dated 1-9-2003 issued by the said Ministry. The Additional District Magistrate in pursuant to the above Memo of the Ministry vide Nilphamary Memo No. J, Pro:/Nilpha:/JM 2003 Kazi Appointment/ 959(5) dated 12-11-2003 informed all concerned regarding the plaintiffs appointment as a Marriage and Divorce Registrar for the said area and the Additional District Magistrate, Nilphamary issued a Public Notification dated 6-12-2003 to this effect. The Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the prayer of the plaintiff appointed him as a permanent Marriage and Divorce Registrar for the aforesaid area under Rule 5(1) of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Rules, 1975. The plaintiff in addition to the said area he upon getting Sanad from the UP Chairman has also been discharging his duties as a Nikah Registrar for No.1 Bhauabari Union since July 19, 1973 AD. The defendant No. 1 is not a valid Kazi and defendant Nos. 2 and 3 have been performing their duties as Nikah Registrars for different Unions under Jaldhaka and Dimpla Police Station but all of them have been registering both marriage and divorce by misguiding the people of 1 No. Golmunda Union and by such they are causing an irreparable loss to the plaintiff. The plaintiff while on 27-2-2004 went to the house of one Sirajul Master to get a marriage registered then some terrorists hired by the defendants assaulted the plaintiff and they also threatened him for not performing his duties as marriage and divorce registrar otherwise they would cause same occurrence as occurred on 27-2-2004 and under the circumstances the plaintiff instituted the suit for permanent injunction against the defendants to restrain them from making any sort of disturbance in discharging the plaintiffs duties in his area. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the plaintiff was none but a fake Kazi and he did not have any valid license either from the local Union Parishad or from the Ministry concerned. The District Registrar appoints a Nikah Registrar after observing necessary formalities by the Ministry for the purpose. The plaintiff was never appointed Marriage and Divorce Registrar by the District Registrar, Nilphamary and the plaintiff even did not deposit Taka 500 and he is not the inhabitant of the concerned Union Parishad. The defendant No. 1 has been legally appointed Kazi for the Golmunda Union since 30-8-2003 and the defendants Nos. 2 and 3 are those of Balagram Union Parishad since 30-12-2002 and 23-7-2002 respectively. They have been discharging as Marriage and Divorce Registrars in accordance with the Rules with the satisfaction of all concerned. The plaintiff on creation of some fake and forged documents is claiming himself to be a Kazi for the area of Golmunda, Balagram and Jhunagasi Chapani Union Parishads. The plaintiff instituted the suit on false allegations and assertions while the defendants made a protest to the said act of the plaintiff. Hence, the suit is liable to be dis-missed with cost. 

 4. At the trial, the plaintiff examined 1(one) witness and the defendant examined 1(one) witness in support of their respective cases. 

 7. Mr Mohammad Nazrul Islam, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner has placed the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below and submits that exhibit-2 is not an appointment letter of the plaintiff in view of rule 5 of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1975. He submits that exhibit-2(ka) is not a permanent appointment letter of the plaintiff as Nikah Registrar as per rules 5(1) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1975. He submits that statement in the plaint and deposition of the plaintiff as PW1 that plaintiff is a Nikah Registrar in Dowabari Union since 1973 as such, he is entitled to get as Nikah Registrar in one Union under rule 10(c) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1975. He submits that the plaintiff failed to prove his case as to cause of action that— 

 “গত ২৭-২-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে বাদী সেরাজুল মাষ্টারের বাড়ীতে বিবাহ রেজিষ্ট্রি করিতে গেলে বিবাদীগণের ভাড়াটিয়া সন্ত্রাসীরা বাদীকে মারধোর করেন এবং দায়িত্ব পালন না করার হুমকি দেন । ২-৩ নং বিবাদীগণ গত ১-৫-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে বাদীর বাড়ীতে আসিয়া গোলমুন্ডা এলাকায় বাদীকে নিকাহ ও তালাক রেজিট্রি করিতে নিষেধ করেন৷ পিডব্লিউ- ১ আনিসুর রহমান তার জবানবব্দীতে বলেন যে, ২৭-২-২০০৪ ইং তারিখ সেরাজুল মাষ্টারের বাড়ীতে বিবাদীরা সন্ত্রাসী দ্বারা আমাকে হুমকি দেয়, মারপিট করে I গত ১-৫-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে পুনরায় বিবাদীরা তাহার কার্যক্রমে বাধা দেন ৷” He submits that the plaintiff has not applied as per rule 5 (a) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1975. He further submits that the plaintiff failed to produce any appointment letter from District Registrar who is chairman of the advisory commit-tee. He also submits that the plaintiff failed to produce any appointment letter from chairman of Golmunda Union. He submits that the court below failed to consider that the plaintiff has been illegally appointed as Nikah Registrar. He lastly submits that both the courts below reached in the decisions on misreading and non-considerations of the evidence and materials on record and, as such, he prayed for to make the rule absolute. In support of his contention he has referred the decisions reported in: (1) 48 DLR (AD) 154, (2) 8 BLC (AD) 77, (3) 59 DLR 448. 

 8. Mr. Md. Mahfuz-ul-Alam, the learned advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 who strongly opposed the rule and submits that both the courts below on consideration of evidence and materials on record rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree. He submits that there is no error of law and misreading and non-consideration of material documents and, as such, no interference is called for by this court in revision. He lastly submits that the plaintiff has been appointed as Nikah Registrar in the year 1973 with Dowabari Union which subsequently changed the name as Golmunda Union vide gazette notification dated 18-11-1996 and since then he has been working Nikah Registrar with Golmunda Union Praishad. In support of his contention he has referred decisions reported in 19 BLC (AD) 139 and 59 DLR 449. 

 11. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiff brought a suit for permanent injunction praying for restraining the defendants from making any sort of disturbance in the functions of the plaintiff as Nikah Registrar in Golmunda Union Parishad. In support of his claim the plaintiff produced exhibit-1(ka) circular dated 6-11-2003 office order dated 12-11-2003 issued from the office of Additional District Magistrate, Nilphamary, Exhibit-2-Temporary appointment for Golmunda Union of the plaintiff issued by Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, exhibit-2(ka) permanent appointment letter dated 1-9-2003 issued by Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, exhibit-3 series চালান ফর্ম্ deposited Taka 325 dated 28-9-2003, চালান ফর্ম্ deposited Taka 250 dated 9-4-2003, চালান ফর্ম্ dated 28-3-2002 deposited Taka 250 চালান ফর্ম্ dated 17-7-2002 deposited Taka 325 চালান ফর্ম্ dated 7-5-2001 Taka 300.25 and চালান ফর্ম্ dated 9-10-2001 deposited Taka 200. The defendant claimed himself as Nikah Registrar in the Golmunda Union got approval for temporary appointment on 30-8-2003 which exhibited and marked as exhibit-(ka-1) by virtue of which the defendant No. 1 was appointed as temporary Nikah Registrar on 29-9-2003. 

 12. In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiff shall have to prove the exclusive possession herein the suit area namely Golmunda Union in order to get a decree. The court may incidentally inquire into prima-facie title are legal right of the parties unless the possession of the plaintiff is clearly established by evidence. It appears that both the courts below have elaborately discussed oral and documentary evidence. The trial court in his findings stated that— 

 15. In view of the above, it appears to me that both the courts below found that the plaintiff was appointed as Nikah Registrar and working since 1973 and also the defendant admitted that plaintiff appointment letter was issued earlier then the defendant. It further appears that the plaintiff has deposited yearly fees by চালান ফর্ম্ (exhibits 3 series) which shows that he has been working as Nikah Registrar. The plaintiff has been working as Marriage and Nikah Registrar for Golmunda Union legally or not and he was appointed as Kazi in accordance with law is not question in the instant case. The question is that whether he has been working as Nikah Registrar in the Golmunda Union since long time and Golmunda Union is under his possession as working place. In a suit for permanent injunction question of title is not material but the possession of the parties is material. It appears that the plaintiff has been able to prove that he has been working as Marriage and Nikah Registrar for Golmunda Union and, as such, he entitled to get permanent injunction. This view finds support in the case of (1) Mohsin Sarker vs Majeda Khatun, reported in 19 BLC (AD) 139 as referred by the learned advocate for the opposite party, where-in their lordships held: 

 "Failure to prove title by the plaintiff in a suit for permanent injunction cannot dis-entitle him to a decree for permanent injunction if he can prove his possession."
